Baseline Copy, Preservation, and Migration Verification

purpose: Establish an immutable V2 starting point copied exactly from the original repository, while defining the rule that the original repository is read-only for the rest of the project.
evidence: Original repository: inoriko920-dev/AI-Automatic-Video-Composer; source branch main.
V2 repository: inoriko920-dev/V2-AI-Video-Composer.
Source main commit inspected during migration: 7d77fc9f724d359c7da6c4796dffce5104740952.
Source root tree SHA: 7abd82b4a69428a0b1bd25a8d992f402cb0a2ff8.
V2 import commit created from an identical root tree SHA: 7abd82b4a69428a0b1bd25a8d992f402cb0a2ff8.
Source snapshot contains 351 blobs, 68 trees, 419 total tree entries, approximately 1.16 MB of tracked blob content.
decisions: The original repository is now archival/reference-only. No feature, experiment, branch, refactor, dependency upgrade, or test-only change is allowed there.
All V2 work must occur only in V2-AI-Video-Composer.
The imported snapshot is the canonical V2 baseline. Any later V2 change must be traceable to a V2 STEP and commit.
Planning documentation must exist before major code changes begin.
tasks: Record baseline commit, tree SHA, dependency pins, release state, CI state, and Windows packaging state.
Create a V2-only planning/documentation directory and a handoff index for future AI sessions.
Define a preservation check that can prove the old repository has not been used as a development target.
Define a reproducible diff command/process comparing V2 baseline against the original snapshot.

Freeze the initial V2 compatibility target: existing project files, current UI behavior, current render output semantics, and current user workflows must remain available unless a later approved plan explicitly changes them.
gate: PASS only when V2 baseline root tree matches the original source root tree.
PASS only when the original repository receives no further V2 development writes.
PASS only when later AI sessions can identify the exact original baseline without guessing.
risks: Accidental edits to the original repo
Losing provenance between V1 and V2
Starting implementation before planning is complete

Legacy Repository Forensic Audit and V2 Scope

purpose: Understand what is already mature, what is fragile, and what should be preserved so V2 improves stability instead of re-implementing working features.
evidence: Current stack: Python 3.12 x64, PySide6/Qt Widgets, FFmpeg/ffprobe CLI, ASS/libass subtitle pipeline, PyInstaller onedir, GitHub Actions.
Architecture already enforces presentation -> application -> domain with infrastructure adapters.
Project state is versioned JSON with atomic save and validation; schema version is currently 2.
Runtime already includes background JobManager, cancellation support, atomic render output, recovery snapshots, secure Gemini key storage, SRT hardening, and malformed input boundaries.
Current animation registry exposes 21 named effects, while the final FFmpeg-native compiler currently provides render-backed motion/alpha/scale/rotation support for a smaller subset.
Previous Windows verification reports hundreds of automated tests plus real FFmpeg and portable build validation.
decisions: Treat existing V2 baseline as a mature product, not a prototype.
Prefer incremental replacement behind interfaces over whole-system rewrites.
Preserve ProjectState compatibility and current user workflows during early V2 waves.
Separate 'registry-visible effect' from 'fully render-backed effect' in planning so unsupported/partial behaviors are not marketed as mature.
tasks: Inventory modules by responsibility: presentation, application/use-cases, domain, render planning, animation compilation, persistence, jobs, providers, paths/tools, packaging, tests.
Classify each area as KEEP, HARDEN, REPLACE-BEHIND-ADAPTER, OPTIONAL-SPIKE, or RETIRE.
Create a feature compatibility matrix for current release behavior versus proposed V2 behavior.
Identify hotspots: large presentation modules, preview/final-render parity boundaries, effect registry/compiler mismatch, media process orchestration, project migration, packaging dependencies.
Identify existing tests that become non-regression gates for V2.
List user-visible contracts that cannot regress: project open/save, scene import, asset binding/relink, subtitles, narration, animation assignments, Gemini Auto, render, portable operation.
gate: PASS when every major subsystem has an explicit KEEP/HARDEN/REPLACE/SPIKE/RETIRE decision.
PASS when current user-visible contracts are listed and mapped to regression tests.
PASS when no major V2 redesign is proposed without naming the existing behavior it replaces.

purpose: Select mature external components only where they measurably improve stability, capability, or maintainability without forcing a license or packaging regression.
evidence: OpenShot/libopenshot latest inspected release: v1.0.1 (2026-09-27), LGPLv3; mature timeline/effects/media library with recent stability and FFmpeg-related work.
MLT latest inspected release: v7.42.0 (2026-10-03), LGPLv2.1; mature multitrack multimedia framework used by video editors.
PyAV latest inspected release: v19.0.1 (2026-10-03), BSD-style license; Pythonic FFmpeg binding with Windows wheels and Python 3.12 support.
OpenTimelineIO is Apache-2.0 and describes itself as a mature editorial interchange framework; useful for timeline data/interchange, not a render engine.
OpenShot/openshot-qt is GPLv3; its application/UI source must not be copied into an MIT-style proprietary-compatible codebase without deliberately accepting GPL obligations.
decisions: Keep FFmpeg CLI as the proven baseline/fallback render path during V2 migration.
Do not copy openshot-qt application code or UI code.
Evaluate libopenshot as an optional render/effects adapter via a contained spike, with legal/packaging review before distribution.
Evaluate MLT as a secondary alternative if libopenshot does not satisfy Windows packaging, deterministic output, or licensing requirements.
Evaluate PyAV for in-process probe/frame/metadata/preview tasks where CLI orchestration is cumbersome; do not assume it should replace FFmpeg CLI final rendering.
Use OpenTimelineIO only if V2's richer timeline/interchange requirements justify it; do not add it merely because it is mature.
tasks: Create a decision matrix: stability, Windows support, Python integration, deterministic rendering, preview capability, effects, keyframes, multitrack, packaging weight, licensing, maintenance activity, testability.
Build isolated proof-of-concept spikes on V2 branches only; each spike must be removable without touching domain contracts.
Measure cold start, preview latency, 1080p render time, memory use, failure behavior, cancellation, and packaging size.
Review redistribution obligations for LGPL libraries and FFmpeg configurations before deciding final bundle policy.
Document reasons for rejection as well as acceptance, so later AI sessions do not repeatedly re-evaluate the same candidates.
gate: PASS when one primary media strategy and one fallback strategy are selected with evidence.
PASS when no GPL application code has been copied into V2.
PASS when packaging/license obligations are documented before dependency adoption.
risks: Replacing deterministic CLI behavior with opaque library behavior

purpose: Evolve the existing modular monolith into a V2 architecture that can host multiple media backends while keeping domain and UI stable.
evidence: Existing architecture already separates presentation, application, domain, and infrastructure.
Current RenderPlan concept is backend-neutral in design, while final compilation is FFmpeg-specific.
JobManager already provides a basic cooperative background execution boundary.
decisions: Retain modular-monolith deployment for V2; do not introduce microservices or Electron solely for novelty.
Introduce explicit MediaBackend/RenderBackend capabilities instead of backend-specific conditionals spread across UI/application code.
Keep domain models free of Qt, subprocess, HTTP, external library objects, and provider SDK types.
Use capability negotiation so UI only exposes effects/features the selected backend can actually preview and render.
tasks: Define ports for ProbeService, PreviewFrameSource, RenderBackend, EffectCompiler, AudioPipeline, SubtitlePipeline, TimelineAdapter, and ToolCapabilityService.
Define immutable backend-neutral render and preview contracts with versioned capability descriptors.
Define adapter boundaries for FFmpeg CLI, optional libopenshot/MLT/PyAV, Qt-native preview, and provider integrations.
Define composition-root wiring and dependency injection conventions.
Define error taxonomy: user input error, media capability error, dependency/tool error, transient provider error, render failure, cancellation, internal invariant violation.
Define observability: structured diagnostics, job lifecycle events, render command summaries without secret leakage.
gate: PASS when the UI can conceptually switch backend capabilities without importing backend libraries.
PASS when final-render determinism and project persistence are independent of a specific optional backend.
PASS when every new dependency has a single adapter ownership point.
risks: Adapter leaking external types into domain
